data.name: Omesh
data.gender_notes: Omesh is used as a male name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Omesh is derived from the Sanskrit word ‘omisha’ meaning ‘intense’, ‘luminescent’, or ‘radiant’. In Hindu mythology, Omesh is associated with the god Vishnu, symbolizing his divine power and brilliance. The name Omesh carries the meaning “Intense, Luminescent” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Sanskrit tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit, Marathi. Parents who choose Omesh usually hope their child will grow to embody intense, luminescent and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.etymology: Omesh belongs to the Sanskrit linguistic tradition and is used in Hindu naming. Its recorded meaning is “Intense, Luminescent.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Omesh total 6, giving a life-path number of 6. Number 6 is linked with Venus and with the qualities of responsibility, care and community.

data.cultural_impact: The name Omesh holds deep cultural significance in ancient India. In the Hindu Mahabharata, a revered Indian epic, a character named Omesh is mentioned. Omesh is a charioteer and a young prince who possesses extraordinary skills in archery and valor. The name Omesh, being derived from the Sanskrit word ‘omisha’, reflects the strong warrior spirit present in Indian culture.
data.spiritual_significance: Spiritually, Omesh embodies the radiant and intense light of God Vishnu. In Hinduism, Vishnu is one of the primary deities, responsible for preserving the universe in balance. Omesh represents the divine power and brilliance of Vishnu, symbolizing the illumination of the soul and the manifestation of divinity in an individual. Additionally, the name Omesh is an invitation to embody the qualities of Vishnu, such as strength, valor, and wisdom, in one’s daily life and actions.
